title: Apex syntax, types, classes, methods, properties, access modifiers, and annotations
objectives: Explain Apex as a strongly typed, object-oriented language that runs on the Salesforce Platform server.
Define a class, method, property, and access modifier using official Apex Developer Guide meanings.
Choose private, protected, public, or global for a method or class and explain why Apex public is not Java public.
Recognize when an annotation or sharing keyword changes visibility or execution, and when a later topic owns the detail.
diagnostic_question: A teammate wants a helper class other packaged Apex can call, another method only this class should use, and a REST entry that outside apps will invoke. Before reading, which access modifiers would you reach for, and what would you check if compilation fails?
definition: Apex is a strongly typed, object-oriented programming language that executes flow and transaction control on the Salesforce Platform server, together with API calls. Classes group methods and variables; access modifiers decide who can see them; annotations mark special platform behavior. ([Apex Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dev_guide.htm); [Access Modifiers](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_access_modifiers.htm))
why_it_matters: Wrong modifiers leak internals across a package or block a SOAP/REST entry. Treating Apex public like Java public is a common interview fail. Interviewers also listen for whether you know a class is metadata deployed to the org, while the records it queries are business data.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an Apex class as a locked workshop on Salesforce's server. Tools on the private bench stay in this room. Public tools are for other workshops in the same building (namespace/package). Global tools are the public loading dock other buildings may call—and the whole workshop must be marked global too. Annotations are stamped work orders: they tell the platform this method is a test, a future job, or an invocable action. Do not confuse the workshop blueprint (the class, metadata) with the parts it machines (records).
deeper_explanation: The Apex Developer Guide describes Apex as strongly typed and object-oriented, running on the platform server with API calls. It is not browser JavaScript and not a substitute for Flow when a declarative path already fits. ([Apex Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dev_guide.htm))

A top-level class declaration must use an access modifier such as public or global. Inner classes default to private if you omit a modifier. You may nest inner classes only one level deep. Optional modifiers include virtual and abstract; with sharing, without sharing, and inherited sharing set the sharing mode of the class. ([Apex Class Definition](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_defining.htm))

Methods and variables default to private: visible only inside the defining class. public in Apex means accessible to Apex in the same application/package (namespace), not 'everyone everywhere' as in Java. global is the Java-like public: any Apex that can see the class may call it, including SOAP API and other packages, and the containing class must also be global. protected is for instance members visible to inner classes and subclasses. ([Access Modifiers](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_access_modifiers.htm))

A method needs a return type (or void), a name, parentheses, at most 32 parameters, and a body. Arguments are passed by value. In API version 65.0 and later, abstract or override methods require protected, public, or global—private is invalid because an implementing class could not see them. ([Class Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_defining_methods.htm); [Access Modifiers](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_access_modifiers.htm))

Annotations such as @IsTest, @AuraEnabled, @InvocableMethod, and @future are later-topic mechanics. This lesson only needs the idea that an annotation is metadata on a class or method that the platform reads. Numeric governor limits belong to APEX-007; async job types belong to APEX-011.

mental_model.analogy: A locked workshop in one building of a campus: private = this room, public = this building's other rooms, global = the campus loading dock, protected = the apprentice rooms that extend this shop.
useful_mapping: method → a named job the workshop can perform
property / member variable → a labeled bin on the bench
public → other Apex in the same namespace/package
global → callers outside that application, including SOAP; class must be global too
annotation → a stamped work order the platform honors
records queried by the class → parts being machined (business data), not the blueprint
where_it_breaks: Apex public is not Java public; interviewers listen for that distinction.
global is a packaging/API contract, not a performance or security shortcut.
with sharing does not replace CRUD/FLS checks; APEX-014 owns that.
The analogy does not encode governor limits, trigger order, or async job choice.

teach_back_prompt: Without saying only 'public means public,' explain Apex private, public, and global to a Java developer, then name one place the Java analogy breaks.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory, write private vs public vs global and one sentence on why Apex public is not Java public.
Given four call sites (same class, same package, managed package, SOAP), pick a modifier for each.
Explain top-level vs inner class modifier rules and where abstract/override private fails on API 65+.
Walk a compile error 'method must be global' from a webservice or REST class without opening notes.
Two-minute interview: class as metadata vs records as data, plus one sharing-keyword boundary.

claims.claim: Apex is a strongly typed, object-oriented language that runs on the Salesforce Platform server with API calls.
Top-level Apex classes must declare public or global; inner classes default to private; inner classes nest only one level.
Methods and variables default to private. Apex public is package/namespace visibility, not Java public. global is required for SOAP/other-application callers and the containing class must be global.
claims.validation: Access Modifiers topic in the Apex Developer Guide.

claims.claim: A method declares a return type or void, at most 32 parameters, and receives arguments by value. From API 65.0, abstract or override methods cannot be private.
claims.validation: Class Methods and Access Modifiers versioned behavior notes.

changed_in_release: API 65.0+ abstract/override methods require protected, public, or global. Reverify the class API version in the target org.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact packaging behavior of @NamespaceAccessible across 2GP versions is out of this topic; confirm in current packaging docs before a managed-package interview deep-dive.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Apex is strongly typed server code. Members default to private. public means same package, not Java public. global is the cross-application contract and the class must be global too. The class is metadata; the rows it queries are data.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from call site: same class, same namespace, subclass, or external SOAP/package. That maps to private, public, protected, or global. I never mark global 'just in case.' Top-level classes need public or global. Inner classes default private. If an abstract method fails to compile on API 65+, I check that it is not private. I separate this lesson from governors, triggers, and Queueable choice.

terminology.precise: A strongly typed, object-oriented language that executes transaction and flow control on the Salesforce Platform server together with API calls.
terminology.example: A LAB_AccountHelper class that updates synthetic LAB_ Account rows in a sandbox.
terminology.non_example: A Lightning web component's JavaScript file, which runs in the browser, not as Apex.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flow: declarative automation that may call Apex but is not Apex syntax.
terminology.boundary: This lesson is language and visibility; governors, SOQL, and async jobs are later Apex topics.

terminology.plain: A named blueprint that holds methods and variables.
terminology.precise: An Apex type you define. Top-level classes must be public or global. Inner classes default to private and nest only one level.
terminology.non_example: A trigger file is not a class definition even though it can contain Apex statements.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: sObject type: a data-model type such as Account, not an Apex class you authored.
terminology.boundary: Class definition and sharing keywords are in scope; trigger frameworks are APEX-009.

terminology.plain: A named action the class can run, with inputs and maybe a return value.
terminology.precise: A member with optional modifiers, a return type or void, up to 32 parameters, and a body. Arguments are passed by value.
terminology.example: public static Decimal LAB_rate(Decimal amount) { return amount; }
terminology.non_example: A formula field is not an Apex method.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Constructor: special initializer, not a general-purpose method with an arbitrary name.
terminology.boundary: Async method annotations such as @future are introduced only as annotations; job choice is APEX-011.

terminology.plain: A typed value stored on the class or an instance.
terminology.precise: A member variable (and related get/set syntax) that holds state for the class or instance; default visibility is private.
terminology.non_example: A custom object field Account.Name is sObject data, not an Apex property.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Custom metadata type field: configuration data, not an Apex member.
terminology.boundary: Instance vs static lifetime continues in later programming topics.

terminology.plain: The keyword that says who is allowed to use a class, method, or variable.
terminology.precise: private (default for members), protected, public (same application/package), or global (any Apex that can see the class, including SOAP). global members require a global class.
terminology.example: private helper vs global webservice method on a global class.
terminology.non_example: A profile permission is authorization for a user, not an Apex access modifier.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: with sharing: record visibility for the running user, not member visibility between Apex types.
terminology.boundary: CRUD/FLS and user mode are APEX-014.

terminology.plain: Visible to other Apex in this package or namespace—not to the whole world.
terminology.precise: The Access Modifiers guide states that Apex public is not the same as Java public; use global when you need Java-like public reach, including SOAP.
terminology.example: public class LAB_InvoiceMath used by other classes in the same unlocked package.
terminology.non_example: Exposing a SOAP API with only public on the class typically fails the 'must be global' contract.
terminology.boundary: @NamespaceAccessible packaging detail is neighboring, not fully specified here.

terminology.plain: Callable from Apex outside this application, including SOAP, if the class is also global.
terminology.precise: global methods and variables can be used by any Apex that has access to the class. The containing class must be global. Webservice methods require a global class.
terminology.example: global class LAB_PricingApi with a global method intended for another package.
terminology.non_example: Marking a one-off helper global 'for convenience' creates a long-lived API surface.
terminology.boundary: Connected-app OAuth is INT-004, not solved by global.

terminology.plain: A stamp on a class or method that tells the platform to treat it specially.
terminology.precise: Apex annotations such as @IsTest change how the platform discovers or runs the member. This lesson treats them as metadata on code, not as a catalog of every annotation.
terminology.example: @IsTest on a test class so it does not count as production Apex in the usual packaging sense.
terminology.non_example: A validation-rule error message is not an Apex annotation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Access modifier: who may call the member, not which platform feature hosts it.
terminology.boundary: Do not memorize an unofficial annotation list here; look up the current Developer Guide when a specific annotation is in play.

mechanics.before: Flow, formula, or validation may still fit
mechanics.after: Apex class candidate or stay declarative
mechanics.observe: Written reason Flow cannot meet the need
mechanics.failure: Writing Apex for a before-save field update Flow already covers

mechanics.after: public or global top-level class in the target API version
mechanics.observe: Class compiles in the sandbox; API version visible on the class

mechanics.after: private, protected, public, or global matched to call sites
mechanics.observe: Call from the intended class or package succeeds; unintended callers fail to compile
mechanics.failure: Using global because public 'felt too small'

when_to_use: When you must name Apex types, methods, and access modifiers in an interview or design review.
When choosing private, public, protected, or global for a helper, subclass hook, or SOAP/package contract.
When a compile error mentions global, abstract, override, or access, and you need the official modifier rules.
When explaining that an Apex class is metadata while SOQL results are business data.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this Apex classes-and-methods lesson as a substitute for Flow vs Apex product choice (AUTO-001) or Queueable vs Batch (APEX-011).
Do not treat Apex access modifiers as a governor-limit catalog (APEX-007) or trigger order-of-execution map (APEX-010).
Do not give a Java visibility lecture that ignores Apex public versus Java public, or that skips class, method, and property syntax.
Do not use Apex class examples to justify production org edits, real customer data, or unapproved deployments.
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Apex Classes, or an sfdx retrieve of classes/*.cls, in a disposable sandbox.
Class header: public/global, optional with sharing, API version on the class metadata.
Method header: modifiers, return type, name, parameter list.
Developer Console or VS Code problems pane for compile errors about access and global.

worked_example.scenario: A sandbox lab needs LAB_DiscountService used by other Apex in the same unlocked package, a private rounding helper, and a global method another package will call for a published contract. No production data.
inputs: Internal roundToCent() that must not leak
Cross-package quote() on a documented API

decisions.because: Only this class should call it; default private already matches.

decisions.decision: Make calculate public on a public class.
decisions.because: Other Apex in this package needs it; Apex public is package/namespace reach.
decisions.rejected: Mark it global without an external contract

decisions.decision: Put quote on a global class as a global method.
decisions.because: The Access Modifiers guide requires global on both member and containing class for cross-application/SOAP-style reach.
decisions.rejected: public class with a global method only

configuration_or_code: public class LAB_DiscountService { private Decimal roundToCent(Decimal n) { return n.setScale(2); } public Decimal calculate(Decimal n) { return roundToCent(n); } }

Separate global class LAB_DiscountApi { global static Decimal quote(Decimal n) { return new LAB_DiscountService().calculate(n); } } — Needs verification of exact packaging/namespace rules in the target package type.
Compile both in sandbox; attempt an illegal caller to prove private fails.
worked_example.output: Same-package Apex compiles against calculate; private helper is invisible; global API class compiles for the documented contract.
verification: Private helper referenced from another class fails to compile.
public calculate is callable from another class in the same package.
Class API version is 67.0 on the metadata.
worked_example.self_explanation: Visibility followed the call site. I did not use global as a default. I treated the classes as metadata and used only LAB_ names.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable Developer sandbox or scratch org; synthetic LAB_ classes only.
starting_state_checks: No production aliases in the class names.
You can create Apex classes in this org.
steps: Create public class LAB_DiscountService with a private helper and a public method.
Create a second class in the same org that calls the public method.
Confirm a call to the private helper from the second class fails.
Read the Access Modifiers guide note on Apex public versus Java public and write one sentence in the class comment.
guided_completion: If the second class compiles against the private helper, the helper is not private.
If you added global without a documented external caller, remove it.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add a protected instance method on a virtual class and a subclass in the same file set; explain who can call it.
evidence: Compile success/failure screenshots or CLI output with LAB_ names only.
One written sentence: Apex public is not Java public.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_ Apex classes from the sandbox.
Do not deploy these classes to production.
hands_on_lab.limitations: This lab does not prove managed-package versioning, SOAP, or governor behavior.

decision_table.signal: Only this class's methods should call the helper.
decision_table.choose: private method or omit the modifier (members default private).
decision_table.not: public or global 'in case we need it later'.
decision_table.why: Default private matches the Access Modifiers guide and keeps the surface small.

decision_table.signal: Other Apex in this unlocked package or namespace must call it.
decision_table.not: global, unless a cross-application or SOAP contract exists.
decision_table.why: Apex public is package/namespace visibility, not Java public.

decision_table.signal: A subclass must override a hook.
decision_table.choose: protected instance method on a virtual or abstract class, API 65+ not private.
decision_table.why: The implementing class cannot see a private abstract method.

decision_table.signal: Another package or SOAP/web service must call this entry.
decision_table.choose: global class and global method (webservice requires global class).
decision_table.not: public class hoping SOAP will ignore the modifier.
decision_table.why: The guide requires global on the member and the containing class for that reach.

limitations: Does not list governor limits, SOQL, or DML patterns.
Does not choose Queueable, Batch, Future, or Scheduled.
Does not replace CRUD/FLS or with sharing design.
Edition, API version, and packaging can change compile rules; reverify the class version.
security_notes: global widens the callable surface; treat it as an API contract.
with sharing is not an access modifier for members.
Never log secrets, session IDs, or real customer data in examples.
common_mistakes: Saying Apex public means the same as Java public.
Omitting global on the class while marking a webservice method global.
Using a private abstract method on API 65+.
Calling the Apex class 'data' and the Account rows 'code'.

troubleshooting.symptom: Compile error that a webservice or global method's class must be global.
check: Mark the top-level class global as well as the member.
Confirm the caller actually needs cross-application reach.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: public on the class is enough for SOAP.

troubleshooting.symptom: Another class cannot see a helper method.
check: The helper is private by default.
Widen to public only if the caller is in-package Apex.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The method is missing; it may be intentionally hidden.

troubleshooting.symptom: Abstract method compile error about access.
check: Class API version is 65.0 or later.
Abstract/override is protected, public, or global.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The method body is the problem.

production_notes: Review global members as published APIs before packaging.
Match class API version to the behaviors you rely on, especially 65+ abstract rules.
No production deployment is authorized by this lesson.

mcqs.prompt: Where does Apex execute according to the Apex Developer Guide?

options.A: On the Salesforce Platform server, with transaction control and API calls
options.B: Only in the browser next to LWC JavaScript
options.C: Only inside a Flow interview, never as its own class

mcqs.rationale: The guide defines Apex as a strongly typed server language that executes flow and transaction control on the platform with API calls.

distractor_explanations.B: LWC JavaScript is client-side; Apex is server-side.
distractor_explanations.C: Flow may invoke Apex; Apex still exists as classes.
distractor_explanations.D: Apex is not limited to Classic.

mcqs.prompt: If you omit an access modifier on an Apex method, what is the default?
mcqs.rationale: Methods and variables default to private—visible only in the defining class.

distractor_explanations.B: public must be specified for same-package reach.
distractor_explanations.D: protected is explicit and used for inheritance.

mcqs.prompt: Why is Apex public not the same as Java public?

options.A: Apex public is same-application/package visibility; Java-like public reach uses global
options.B: Apex public is always world-visible and Java public is package-private
options.D: Apex public only applies to inner classes

mcqs.rationale: The Access Modifiers guide says Apex public was defined differently from Java to keep applications separate; use global for Java-like public reach.

distractor_explanations.C: public is a standard Apex modifier.
distractor_explanations.D: public applies to classes and members, not only inner classes.

mcqs.prompt: A webservice method is declared global. What else does the Access Modifiers / class-definition guidance require?

options.A: The containing class must also be global
options.C: The class must be an inner class

mcqs.rationale: If a method is global, the outer class must be global. Webservice methods require a global class.

distractor_explanations.C: Top-level global classes are the usual container.
distractor_explanations.D: Return type is independent of global.

mcqs.prompt: What access modifier must a top-level Apex class use?

options.D: None; top-level classes default to private

mcqs.rationale: Top-level class declarations must use public or global. private is for inner classes (or @IsTest top-level test classes in the cited inner-class note).

distractor_explanations.B: private is not the required top-level production-class modifier.
distractor_explanations.C: protected is for instance members, not the usual top-level class modifier.
distractor_explanations.D: Top-level classes cannot omit the modifier the way inner classes can.

mcqs.prompt: How deep can Apex inner classes nest?
mcqs.rationale: You can only have inner classes one level deep.

distractor_explanations.B: Java-style deep nesting is not allowed.
distractor_explanations.C: The documented limit is one level.
distractor_explanations.D: Inner classes are allowed, with a depth of one.

mcqs.prompt: On API version 65.0+, which is invalid for an abstract method?

options.A: Leaving it private (the default) so implementers cannot see it
options.B: Declaring it public on an abstract class
options.D: Declaring it global on a global abstract class

mcqs.rationale: From API 65.0, abstract or override methods require protected, public, or global. Private is invalid because implementers could not access it.

distractor_explanations.D: global is allowed when the class is global.

mcqs.prompt: What is the documented maximum number of input parameters for an Apex method?
mcqs.rationale: A method can have only 32 input parameters.

distractor_explanations.C: 255 is not the method-parameter cap in this guide section.
distractor_explanations.D: There is a documented maximum of 32.

mcqs.prompt: Apex method arguments are passed how?

options.B: Always by reference like Java objects exclusively

mcqs.rationale: The Class Methods topic covers passing arguments by value (and discusses the related reference behavior for some types in that same chapter). The interview-safe official headline is pass by value as documented.

distractor_explanations.B: Do not import Java argument rules wholesale.
distractor_explanations.C: Apex does not use Python-style pass-by-name.
distractor_explanations.D: Methods may take up to 32 parameters.

mcqs.prompt: You need a hook only subclasses should override. Which modifier matches the Access Modifiers guide?

options.A: protected on an instance method of a virtual or abstract class
options.C: global on an inner class by default

mcqs.rationale: protected is for instance methods and member variables visible to inner classes and subclasses.

distractor_explanations.B: private static is not an override hook for subclasses.
distractor_explanations.C: Inner classes default private, not global.
distractor_explanations.D: Triggers are not class access modifiers.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates Apex class metadata from business data?

options.A: Deploying LAB_DiscountService.cls does not insert Account records
options.B: Every Apex class is stored as an Account row
options.C: SOQL results are metadata and the .cls file is business data

mcqs.rationale: The class is code metadata. Records queried or inserted are business data. This is the same metadata-vs-data split used across the handbook.

distractor_explanations.D: OWD is a sharing setting, not an Apex modifier.

mcqs.prompt: A requirement is a simple field update on the same record before save. What should you consider before writing an Apex class?

options.A: A before-save record-triggered Flow may already fit; Apex is not automatic
options.B: Always write a global Apex class first
options.D: Validation rules cannot run on save

mcqs.rationale: AUTO-001 owns tool choice. This lesson still expects you not to default to Apex for same-record updates Flow can do.

distractor_explanations.B: global is a visibility contract, not a default architecture.
distractor_explanations.C: Apex and Flow both update records on the server.
distractor_explanations.D: Validation rules are a separate save-order concern.

One level deep. Inner classes default to private.

flashcards.back: No. It sets record-sharing mode for the class. Member visibility is private/public/global/protected.

Other Apex in this package must call it?

interview_questions.question: What is Apex, and where does it run?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex is Salesforce's strongly typed, object-oriented language. It runs on the platform server, not in the browser, and participates in transactions and API calls.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote the Developer Guide: Apex executes flow and transaction control on the Salesforce Platform server. I contrast it with LWC JavaScript and with Flow. I mention that a class is metadata we deploy, while the records it queries are data. I do not recite unofficial governor numbers unless I am in the limits topic.
interview_questions.example: LAB_DiscountService.calculate runs in a sandbox transaction when another Apex class calls it.
tradeoffs: Apex vs Flow for the same requirement
follow_ups: When would you refuse to write Apex?
What API version is on the class?

interview_questions.question: Explain private, public, and global in Apex.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Members default to private. public is other Apex in this package. global is cross-application and SOAP, and the class must be global too. Apex public is not Java public.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map each modifier to a call site. Same class: private. Same namespace/package: public. Subclass hook: protected. Other package or webservice: global on both member and class. I mention the guide's explicit Java comparison so the interviewer hears I did not import Java rules blindly.
interview_questions.example: private roundToCent, public calculate in-package, global quote for a published API.
follow_ups: What happens if only the method is global?

interview_questions.question: A SOAP/webservice method compiles except for an error that the class must be global. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Mark the containing top-level class global as well. Webservice methods require a global class. Then confirm we actually need that external contract.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat the error as a pairing rule from the Access Modifiers and class-definition topics: global members live on global classes. I check whether SOAP is required; if the caller is only in-package Apex, I would drop webservice/global and use public instead. I would not 'fix' it by making every helper global.
interview_questions.example: global class LAB_PricingApi { webservice static Decimal quote(Decimal n) { ... } }
tradeoffs: Published SOAP surface vs in-package public method
follow_ups: How would you version this later?

interview_questions.question: An abstract method fails to compile on a class set to API 65. What do you check first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Whether the abstract method is private. From API 65.0, abstract and override methods need protected, public, or global.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I read the class API version. If it is 65 or later, a missing modifier defaults to private, which is illegal for abstract/override because implementers cannot see it. I add protected or public as the design requires. I do not blindly lower the API version to hide the error without a versioning plan.
interview_questions.example: abstract class LAB_Hook { abstract protected void beforeSave(); }
tradeoffs: Staying on API 65+ vs pinning an older version
follow_ups: Can inner classes be abstract in the same way?
weak_answer_warnings: Blaming the method body instead of visibility

interview_questions.question: When would you not write an Apex class at all?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a formula, validation rule, or before-save Flow already implements the same-record rule safely. Apex is a tool, not the default.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate this language topic from AUTO-001, but interviewers still expect judgment. Same-row updates, simple requiredness, and many approvals are declarative. I write Apex when I need transaction control, complex branching, or a reusable service other Apex must call. I still apply access modifiers correctly when I do write it.
interview_questions.example: Updating a LAB_ status field on the same Opportunity can be before-save Flow; a multi-object split with callouts is not this lesson's job but is not a formula.

interview_questions.question: How do you explain an Apex class versus the records it queries?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The class is metadata we deploy. Account rows it queries or inserts are business data. Deploying a class does not load records.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep the same split as DATA-001 and DEVOPS-001. Source control owns the .cls. Data tools own records. Tests create synthetic LAB_ data; they do not prove production data migration. Access modifiers on the class do not replace sharing or CRUD.
interview_questions.example: sfdx deploy of LAB_DiscountService.cls leaves Account empty until a test or loader inserts LAB_ rows.

interview_questions.question: Another class cannot call your helper. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check whether the helper is private. If the caller is in-package Apex, public may be enough. If it is another package, you need a global contract, not a quiet public.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce the compile error. I look at the helper modifier, the caller's namespace, and whether we intended an API. I do not flip to global to silence the error. I also check inner-class defaults and whether someone expected Java public behavior.
interview_questions.example: LAB_OtherService calling LAB_DiscountService.roundToCent fails because roundToCent is private.
follow_ups: How do you test the intended caller?
Would you use inner classes here?

interview_questions.question: A Java developer joins the team. What Apex visibility trap do you teach first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex public is not Java public. If they need world-like reach, that is global, and it is an API decision.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show the Access Modifiers paragraph that states the difference explicitly. I walk three call sites on a whiteboard: same class, same package, other package. I add that top-level classes must be public or global, inner classes default private, and abstract methods cannot hide as private on API 65+. I warn that global is hard to shrink later.
interview_questions.example: They mark a helper public expecting other managed packages to call it; those packages still cannot see it without a global/namespace design.
tradeoffs: Java muscle memory vs Apex packaging
follow_ups: How do 2GP versions interact? (Mark needs verification.)
weak_answer_warnings: Teaching Java visibility as if it were Apex
